IHE Integration Profiles and How to Require Them in a Purchase

Unit 1: Imaging Informatics Foundations. Lesson 5 of 65 in CIIP Academy.

Your hospital is buying a new PACS. The vendor says it is "standards based." Your RFP needs wording that turns that claim into something you can test and hold them to.

What IHE is

IHE does not write new standards. It publishes integration profiles that say how existing standards (DICOM, HL7, web services) are combined to solve a named workflow problem. A profile defines actors (roles such as the image manager) and transactions (the messages between actors). Vendors prove it at the Connectathon, and publish an integration statement that lists which actors they support.

The profiles that matter most

Profile                       Problem it solves
Scheduled Workflow            order to report with consistent data
Patient Information Reconciliation   demographics fixed after an unidentified exam
Consistent Presentation of Images    same grayscale look on every display
Key Image Note                flag significant images with a comment
Portable Data for Imaging     studies on CD, DVD, or USB with an index
XDS-I.b                       cross-enterprise sharing of imaging
Invoke Image Display          open the viewer on the right study
Radiation Exposure Monitoring dose records to a registry
Audit Trail and Node Authentication   central audit and encrypted links
Consistent Time               every clock set from one source

Requiring profiles in an RFP

Name the profile, the actor, and the role you need: for example "image manager and image archive actors for Scheduled Workflow." Ask for the integration statement, and ask that each claimed actor be demonstrated in your test environment before acceptance.

Exam tip: IHE profiles are how you turn "supports standards" into a requirement. Name the profile and the actor, request the integration statement, and verify in testing.
Remember
IHE profiles combine existing standards into named workflows with actors and transactions, and a good RFP names the profile and actor and then tests the vendor's integration statement.
Deeper explanation

IHE Integration Profiles and How to Require Them in a Purchase, explained slowly

From problem to profile

Profiles are most useful when you start from a problem and ask which profile fixes it. This table is the map the exam wants you to carry.

Problem you have                                   Profile to require
Orders, images, and reports disagree on data       Scheduled Workflow
Trauma patient scanned before registration         Patient Information Reconciliation
Same image looks different on two displays         Consistent Presentation of Images
Radiologist needs to flag images for clinician     Key Image Note
Patient leaves with images on a disc               Portable Data for Imaging
Outside hospital needs your studies                XDS-I.b cross-enterprise sharing
EMR link opens the viewer on the wrong study       Invoke Image Display
Need to track dose across scanners                 Radiation Exposure Monitoring
Auditor asks who viewed a study                    Audit Trail and Node Authentication
Audit time stamps disagree between systems         Consistent Time

Actors and transactions

Each profile defines actors such as an order placer, an order filler, an image manager, and an image archive. The actors exchange defined transactions. A product that claims a profile must claim specific actors, and the integration statement lists them.

Writing it into an RFP

Poor wording: "The system shall support IHE." Good wording: "The system shall support the Scheduled Workflow profile as image manager and image archive, the Patient Information Reconciliation profile as image manager, and the Audit Trail and Node Authentication profile as secure node, as shown in the vendor's integration statement. Each claimed actor shall be demonstrated in the buyer's test environment before acceptance."

Worked example

A vendor's integration statement lists Scheduled Workflow as an image display actor only. The RFP required the image manager and archive actors. The gap is found before contract signing, which is the point of requesting the statement. The buyer asks the vendor to commit in writing to the missing actors with a date, or scores the bid lower.

The Connectathon

Vendors test against one another at an IHE Connectathon. A product that has passed is more likely to interoperate, but your acceptance test on your own network still decides.
